question: What is vendor-managed inventory?
html:
Vendor-managed inventory (VMI) means Thomas Scientific, as the supplier, monitors and restocks the consumables a lab keeps on its shelves, instead of the lab placing every order itself. The customer agrees the items and stock levels. We track usage and replenish before anything runs out.

How it works in practice

  • Agree the list. The lab and Thomas set which products are covered, such as gloves, pipette tips and reagents, and the minimum and maximum quantities for each.
  • Watch consumption. Usage is tracked through counts, scans or connected ordering.
  • Replenish automatically. When stock nears the minimum, Thomas ships a refill without waiting for a purchase order to start.
  • Review together. Usage trends inform future stock levels and forecasts.

Where it sits in the plan

VMI is one of the named levers in the growth plan. That plan aims to move Thomas from distributor to lab supply-chain company, alongside target-account selling, punchout ordering, private label and specialty verticals (Thomas Scientific growth plan).

LeverRole in the plan
Punchout and digital orderingTable stakes for large lab buyers
Private label, AI pricingMargin through mix
VMIMakes accounts sticky
AI forecasting agentsSupports replenishment and account health

The plan says margin "has to come from mix," and it groups VMI with private label and pricing as the tools that hold onto accounts (Thomas Scientific growth plan).

What we cannot yet say

The context does not give the number of VMI accounts, VMI revenue share or retention lift. Answering those would need:

  • A list of current VMI accounts and the revenue tied to them.
  • Renewal and churn rates for VMI customers versus non-VMI customers.
  • Service and inventory carrying costs per VMI site.

Sequencing matters

Every lever sits behind liquidity and refinancing. The first-lien loan matures December 14, 2027, and estimated leverage is 7–10x (est.) (Thomas Scientific public filings). VMI ties up inventory and working capital, so a rollout needs to be paced against cash. The growth plan's 36-month roadmap targets about 3,000 Pursue and Nurture sites under named coverage. That makes those accounts the natural VMI candidates (est.; assumption, not a forecast).

For a portfolio company refinancing on its growth story, VMI is one of the clearest ways to show lenders that revenue is recurring and hard to dislodge, not commodity order flow.

Next actions

  1. Pull the current VMI account list, the revenue on it, and churn compared with non-VMI accounts.
  2. Model the working-capital cost per VMI site before expanding, and gate any rollout to the refinancing timeline.
  3. Pilot VMI with a small set of high-scoring Pursue sites already under named coverage.
  4. Link VMI usage data to the planned AI forecasting and account-health agents.
